The actual existing recursion admits a complete elementary proof; no Bogovskii, inf-sup, L2 pressure result, or new substantial lemma is needed.
findings.proof_review: For Jg(x1,x')=integral_a1^x1 g, Cauchy-Schwarz yields ||Jg||2 <= ell ||g||2, partial1 Jg=g, partialj Jg=J partialj g; thus ||Jg||H1 <= sqrt(1+ell^2)||g||H1. The marginal H satisfies ||H||H1 <= sqrt(ell)||h||H1. Multiplication G -> theta1 G obeys ||theta1 G||H1 <= B||G||H1, B^2=||theta1||2^2+||theta1'||2^2. The same recursion therefore obeys C_Omega^2=(1+ell^2)(1+B sqrt(ell))^2+B^2 ell C_OmegaPrime^2. One-dimensional primitives start the finite induction. This constant depends only on fixed sides and bumps. Compact support, zero-mean endpoint cancellation and all-order test continuity remain proved by the original argument.
findings.consumer_repair: Use the strengthened F4 directly in pressure3.1; independently construct the normalized bump instead of referring to unexposed supplier formulas. Give the complete continuous-extension argument to H0^1.
